subject: geography
title: Ecosystems Adventure: Global Biomes
welcome_lead: From scorching deserts to icy tundra — climate controls where the great biomes live.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography Global biomes — rainforest, desert, tundra, savanna, deciduous forest.
final_note: You can now locate the major world biomes and explain why they're where they are.

concepts.def: Large region with similar climate, plants and animals
Hot wet biome near the equator — huge biodiversity
Dry biome ~30°N/S — under high pressure belts
Tropical grassland with wet and dry seasons
Temperate biome — trees drop leaves in winter

walkthroughs.body_html:
The sun's energy hits the equator most directly — hot and wet here.

At ~30°N and 30°S, sinking dry air creates the world's great deserts (Sahara, Atacama, Australian outback).

Towards the poles, biomes get colder: deciduous forest → coniferous (taiga) → tundra → ice.

Near the equator (Amazon, Congo, SE Asia).

Hot (25-30°C year-round) and wet (>2000mm rain). Layered structure: emergents, canopy, under-canopy, forest floor.

Contains over 50% of the world's terrestrial species despite covering only ~6% of land.

Found ~30° latitude (Sahara, Arabia, Mojave) under permanent high pressure.

Less than 250mm rainfall per year. Huge temperature range — scorching day, freezing night.

Plants (cacti) have waxy skin and deep roots. Animals are often nocturnal.

mcqs.q: Why are the world's great hot deserts found around 30°N and 30°S?
options: Tectonic plate boundaries
Sinking dry air from high pressure belts
Ocean currents flow there
Glacial melt creates dryness

mcqs.q: Which biome is characterised by PERMAFROST?
options: Tropical rainforest
Tundra
Savanna
Hot desert

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
Climate change only happens in summer.

mcqs.q: What weather does an anticyclone (high pressure system) bring?
options: Descending air warms and dries, suppressing cloud formation — so anticyclones bring clear, settled weather: hot in summer, cold and frosty in winter.
Climate change only happens in summer.
High pressure brings stormy weather because the air pushes down hard.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the tundra and the taiga biomes?
options: Climate change only happens in summer.
Tundra is treeless cold biome (too cold and permafrost-dominated for trees), while taiga (boreal forest) is the band of coniferous forest just south of the tundra in subarctic latitudes.
Tundra and taiga are the same biome with different names.
Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Savanna”?
options: Tropical grassland with wet and dry seasons
Dry biome ~30°N/S — under high pressure belts
Temperate biome — trees drop leaves in winter
Hot wet biome near the equator — huge biodiversity

options: Temperate biome — trees drop leaves in winter
Tropical grassland with wet and dry seasons
Large region with similar climate, plants and animals
Dry biome ~30°N/S — under high pressure belts

mcqs.q: Approximately what maximum annual rainfall (mm) defines a hot desert?

numericals.q: Approximately what maximum annual rainfall (mm) defines a hot desert?
numericals.hint: Less than a quarter of a metre per year.
